summary.headline: Sambhv Q1 FY27 revenue INR732 crore (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR100 crore, PAT INR56 crore; FY27 EBITDA/ton guided INR7,500-8,500.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the highest-ever quarter for revenue, EBITDA and PAT, with revenue up 31%, EBITDA up 31% and PAT up 70% YoY. Sales volume rose 16% YoY and value-added volume rose 27%, with EBITDA per ton of about INR10,000 excluding sponge iron. The Kuthrel stainless CR coil debottlenecking doubled capacity to 116,000 tpa, and the Kesda greenfield project is guided for Q4 FY27 commissioning. Management guided FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of 10-15% over FY26, and flagged softer MS pricing and stainless steel import competition as the main headwinds.

segments.name: MS ERW pipes and tubes
segments.commentary: Q1 net realisation about INR60,000/ton, guided to about INR58,000/ton in Q2. Capacity utilisation above 65% against a market norm of about 70%.

segments.name: GP pipe and coil
segments.commentary: Q1 net realisation about INR75,000/ton, guided to INR72,000-73,000/ton in Q2. Operating above 90% utilisation.

segments.name: Stainless steel (SS 200 / SS 300)
segments.commentary: Q1 realisation about INR1,40,000/ton for SS 200 and INR2,00,000-2,10,000/ton for SS 300; Q2 guided to INR1,30,000 and about INR2,00,000. Stainless CR coil margin guided at INR15,000-16,000/ton; utilisation about 60% after the Kuthrel doubling to 116,000 tpa.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA per ton guided at INR7,500-8,500 (weighted average), and Q2 FY27 at INR7,500-8,500.
FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of 10-15% over FY26; FY26 operating EBITDA base cited as about INR270 crore.
FY27 sales volume guided at 10-15% above FY26; segment volumes: MS pipes 230,000-240,000 t, GP pipe and coil about 90,000 t, stainless CR coil about 60,000 t (about 400,000 t total value-added).
FY27 margin guided at about 12% with a 1-2% standard deviation; PAT margin guided at about 6% with a 1% standard deviation.
FY28 EBITDA per ton guided above INR8,000; FY28 revenue cited at about INR4,500 crore.
MS pipe prices expected to fall a further 3-5% this financial year; stainless steel pricing expected to soften as QCO relaxation lets in imports.
capex_capacity: Kesda greenfield (Phase 1, 360,000 tpa stainless CR coil) at INR930 crore, targeted for trial run and production in Q4 FY27; total stainless capacity to reach 476,000 tpa by Q4 2027.
Kuthrel Unit 2 stainless CR coil debottlenecking completed; capacity doubled from 58,000 to 116,000 tpa, with consent to operate now in place.
Captive power plant of INR200 crore plus DFT pipe mill (150,000 t) with INR100 crore spend in FY27 and INR100 crore in FY28; DFT mill expected to lift MS capacity to about 500,000 t by Q2 2028.
8 MW rooftop solar at Kuthrel for INR25 crore (INR10-12 crore in FY27, balance in FY28), expected to reduce power cost.

Total captive power to reach about 88-90 MW from 25 MW today, with a 2030 target of about 150 MW; estimated power cost saving of INR180-200 crore. Finished capacity target of over 2 million tpa by 2030.
Peak debt by end FY27 cited as INR800-850 crore term debt and INR200-300 crore working capital; cost of debt 7.5-8%.
Working capital need of about INR200 crore in FY28 (about 35% utilisation) rising to INR300 crore in FY29 (60-65% utilisation) for Kesda.
demand_pricing: Management expects MS pipe prices to stabilise after a further 3-5% decline this financial year; cited a lackluster demand environment elsewhere but said Sambhv's volume of about 20,000-24,000 t/month is not much affected.

Stainless steel: QCO framework relaxed and shipping delays from the war situation; Chinese stainless cost now broadly at par with Indian cost, so pricing competition expected to rise once shipments normalise.
Nickel exposure limited: about 90% of production is 200-series, sourced from nickel scrap and alloys.
Stainless co-branding: 28 MoU partners (18 added in Q1); about 1,200 t supplied currently, targeted at about 2,500 t by year end.
Net realisations for Q1 and Q2 guided as above; management said segment-wise realisation is not rising much, with overall realisation rising from the SS mix shift.
Engineers India Limited and Chennai Metro Rail approvals received during the quarter, supporting institutional sales.

qa_highlights.question: What will peak debt, finance cost and cost of debt look like after Kesda?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt by end FY27 of about INR800-850 crore term debt and INR200-300 crore working capital; cost of debt currently 7.5-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kesda Q4 FY27 timeline achievable through monsoon?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is optimistic on trial run and production by Q4 FY27; substructure is done and superstructure is advanced, with machinery installation proceeding in monsoon.

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the INR100 crore warrant issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Funds for capex at the holding company and the wholly owned subsidiary Sambhv Tubes, working capital for Kesda, and promoter contribution toward the solar, DFT mill and captive power projects; promoters and management to participate.

qa_highlights.question: Why co-branding for stainless pipes instead of direct sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 800-900 small pipe makers sell regionally, so co-branding with 28 partners builds Sambhv awareness; Sambhv sells only CR coil, not pipe.

qa_highlights.question: Stainless CR coil margin and HR coil margin?
qa_highlights.answer: CR coil margin about INR15,000-16,000/ton; HR coil expected at INR12,000-13,000/ton once Kesda starts, and lower initially.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA growth guided at only 10-15% given the stainless ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: Stainless production has peaked, so volume looks flat; management expects pricing softness in stainless as QCO relaxation allows imports, and is guiding conservatively.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital needs and capex schedule?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital of about INR200 crore in FY28 and INR300 crore in FY29 for Kesda; Kesda INR930 crore mostly in FY27, with power plant and DFT mill spread over FY27 and FY28.

risks_watch: Kesda Phase 1 (360,000 tpa stainless CR coil, INR930 crore) must hit trial run and production by Q4 FY27; management says machinery installation is proceeding through monsoon.
Stainless pricing risk: QCO relaxation and easing shipping constraints could bring Chinese and other imports back, with management expecting softer stainless margins once shipments normalise.
MS pipe prices guided to fall a further 3-5% this financial year; Q2 FY27 realisations guided lower for MS pipe (about INR58,000/ton from INR60,000) and GP pipe, with monsoon softness flagged.
Debt build-up: peak term debt of INR800-850 crore and working capital of INR200-300 crore by end FY27 at a 7.5-8% cost of debt, plus INR100 crore warrant issue to promoters.

Stainless utilisation at about 60% after the Kuthrel doubling to 116,000 tpa, and the ramp-up of Kesda to 35% utilisation in FY28 and 60-65% in FY29, will determine whether the capacity adds volume and margin.

Our debottlenecking initiative has doubled our production capacity from 58,000 tons per annum to 1,16,000 tons per annum.
So, yes, pricing wise, it will be softer in stainless steel margin.
I don't want to counter my industry peers, so I will go with them.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on project timelines, with specific numbers given readily on capacity, pricing and capex. Noticeably cautious on FY27 guidance: management called the 10-15% EBITDA growth conservative and said stainless pricing will soften, and it deflected on Q2 industry realisations and on sponge iron requirements for the expansion.
